'''MyMaths''' is a subscription-based [[mathematics]] website which can be used on [[interactive whiteboard]]s or by students and teachers at home.<ref>{{cite book |last=Cowan|first=Pamela| page=112|title=Teaching Mathematics: A Handbook for Primary and Secondary School Teachers|publisher=Psychology Press | year=2006| isbn=9780415335171}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=Basic Maths for Dummies |last=Beveridge |first=Colin |publisher=John Wiley & Sons| year=2011|page=314|isbn=9781119975618}}</ref> It is owned and operated by [[Oxford University Press]], who acquired the site in 2011. As of February 2021, MyMaths has over 4 million student users in over 70 countries worldwide.<ref>{{cite web|title=MyMaths FAQs|url=https://www.mymaths.co.uk/help.html|url-status=live|access-date=26 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210226030311/https://www.mymaths.co.uk/help.html|archive-date=26 February 2021}}</ref>

==Usage and Cost==
MyMaths operates a [[subscription]] model, where schools must pay to access the service. There is a cost of £392 for primary schools or £695 for secondary schools, per annum and not including [[VAT]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Subscribe|publisher=MyMaths|url=https://www.mymaths.co.uk/subscribe.html|accessdate=21 April 2023}}</ref> Limited resources are available as a free trial. Schools receive an institution username and password, allowing students to access content on the site, and can set up profiles for individual students, enabling teachers to track the progress and grades achieved on homework.<ref>{{cite web|title=My Portal|publisher=MyMaths|url=https://support.mymaths.co.uk/student-support/secondary-students/my-portal-secondary/|date=24 September 2020 |accessdate=20 April 2021}}</ref>

==Content==
MyMaths has a wide range of curriculum materials and resources aimed at students in primary and secondary schools, covering content from [[Key Stage 1|KS1]] foundations to [[A-Level]] [[Further Mathematics]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Home|publisher=MyMaths|url=https://www.mymaths.co.uk/|accessdate=20 April 2021}}</ref><ref name="1c">{{cite web|title=MyiMaths|publisher=HeyGrove (Somerset Educational Institution)|url=http://www.haygrove.somerset.sch.uk/document_1.aspx?id=0:61412&id=0:35714&id=0:35701&id=0:35626 |date=7 September 2011 |accessdate=22 May 2012}}</ref> However, it does not cover all topics. Each topic consists of a 'Lesson' which teaches the methods and provides interactive examples, as well as an "Online homework" task which provides and automatically marks practice questions. "Booster packs" for revision purposes and simplistic games are also available.

Whilst MyMaths only provides content for UK examinations, the sister site MyiMaths provides content for international qualifications.

==Flash==
MyMaths was originally constructed in [[Adobe Flash|Flash]], but most content has now been translated into [[HTML]] or other standards as of January 2021. 28 games and some other content was replaced or deleted after widespread support for Flash was ended at the end of 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=MyMaths and Flash |date=13 May 2019 |publisher=MyMaths|url=https://support.mymaths.co.uk/technical-support/what-mymaths-content-has-been-updated/|accessdate=20 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Important update – retirement of remaining Flash content on MyMaths |publisher=MyMaths|url=https://www.mymaths.co.uk/news/2020/12/04/retirement-of-flash-content.html|accessdate=20 April 2021}}</ref>

==Impact==
An impact study undertaken by Oxford University Press — the owners of the website — conducted 22 interviews with teachers, finding that using MyMaths saved teachers between 15 minutes and 5 hours a week, with an average of around 2 hours.<ref>{{cite web|title=To what extent does using MyMaths save teachers time? |url=https://www.mymaths.co.uk/files/oxford_impact_study_mymaths.pdf|accessdate=20 April 2021}}</ref>
